New evidence
- Buhari’s Bloomberg Q&A was a self-evaluation of his tenure: he claimed Nigeria was left in a better state, corruption was less hidden, recovered funds were flowing back, and insurgents no longer controlled territory. That is useful as direct ruler speech, but it is not independently verified and sits next to multiple contrary signals in the record. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Nigerian President Buhari’s Q&A With Bloomberg News: Transcript","publisher":"The State House, Abuja","publication_date":"2022-06-21","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/nigerian-president-buharis-qa-with-bloomberg-news-transcript/","claim":"Buhari said Nigeria was left in a better state, with corruption more exposed, recovered funds returning, and insurgents no longer holding territory.","locator":"Q1 response, lines 30-33 and 46-48","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary transcript of Buhari’s own written responses published by the presidency; the claim is direct self-report rather than independently checked fact.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Direct 2022 end-of-tenure self-assessment within the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Buhari statement; high attribution, but the truth of the claims is not established by the source alone.","contrary_evidence":["Other 2022 sources in this dossier show patronage, censorship, and alleged lopsided appointments.","The statement is self-serving and not an independent audit."],"lenses":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"]}`
- Buhari told the EFCC not to be used for partisan politics or personal disputes and said the anti-graft fight should be grounded in transparency, accountability, and rule of law. This is again self-presentation, but it is a concrete ethical posture he publicly endorsed. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"President Buhari Cautions EFCC on Political Interference, Commends Recovery of Looted Funds","publisher":"The State House, Abuja","publication_date":"2022-03-25","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-cautions-efcc-on-political-interference-commends-recovery-of-looted-funds/","claim":"Buhari urged EFCC to avoid partisan politics and personal disputes and framed anti-corruption work as a transparency-and-accountability effort under the rule of law.","locator":"paras. 27-44","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential speech with clear attributable language and dated publication.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Buhari speech; it reflects his stated integrity stance, not proof of practice.","contrary_evidence":["The same year also saw criticisms of nepotism and censorship.","The source does not show how the EFCC message was implemented in practice."],"lenses":["7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"]}`
- In the cabinet-sendoff speech, Buhari said resigning ministers had served the nation with dignity, said his cabinet selection had sought the best and most competent, and thanked appointees for complying with his directive. This is a useful record of a concrete anti-incumbency rule he imposed on his own team. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"President Buhari’s Speech at the Valedictory Session for Appointees Leaving the Cabinet to Pursue Political Ambition","publisher":"The State House, Abuja","publication_date":"2022-05-13","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buharis-speech-at-the-valedictory-session-for-appointees-leaving-the-cabinet-to-pursue-political-ambition/","claim":"Buhari said departing ministers had served sacrificially, said cabinet selection aimed to produce the best and most competent, and thanked them for complying with his resignation directive.","locator":"paras. 30-32 and 43-49","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential speech published the same day, with explicit language on appointments and resignation compliance.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022 and tied to the election-year cabinet resignations.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Buhari directive and public praise of compliance; high attribution.","contrary_evidence":["The cabinet was still widely seen as patronage-heavy by critics.","The speech is self-described and does not independently verify competence or honesty."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.8","7B.9"]}`
- Buhari’s May 2022 directive required cabinet members seeking office to resign by 16 May, and Reuters reported ten ministers resigned while the government said the goal was to prevent them from benefiting from office. This is one of the clearest positive integrity signals in the dossier. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Nigeria’s Buhari asks ministers with political ambition to resign","publisher":"Al Jazeera / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-05-11","url":"https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/5/11/nigerias-buhari-asks-ministers-with-political-ambition-to-resign","claim":"Buhari directed cabinet members seeking elective office to resign by May 16, 2022, to avoid benefiting from their government positions; the report says at least five cabinet members were seeking office.","locator":"paras. 66-74","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting is strong for the directive and resignations, though this is still a report of executive action rather than a legal record.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exactly within the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct presidential directive communicated through the information minister; attribution is strong.","contrary_evidence":["The initial instruction did not clearly cover every political appointee outside the cabinet.","Emefiele was initially left in a gray zone, suggesting uneven enforcement."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.8","7B.9"]}`
- The January 2022 NNPC Limited board appointment is the strongest clean example of formal appointments: Buhari named a board and management team under the Petroleum Industry Act, with members from multiple geopolitical zones and defined executive roles. That is a plausible positive signal on professionalized appointments, though the press release alone cannot prove merit or absence of patronage. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"President Buhari Appoints Board and Management of NNPC Limited","publisher":"The State House, Abuja","publication_date":"2022-01-05","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-buhari-appoints-board-and-management-of-nnpc-limited/","claim":"Buhari appointed the NNPC Limited board and management under the Petroleum Industry Act, naming members from multiple geopolitical zones and assigning executive roles.","locator":"paras. 27-37","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary presidential appointment notice with full roster and legal basis.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct presidential appointment under Buhari’s authority.","contrary_evidence":["The document itself does not prove competence or absence of patronage.","Later criticism of Buhari’s broader patronage patterns remains relevant."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.9"]}`
- BusinessDay’s 2022 critique makes the nepotism problem concrete: it says Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu’s appointment as managing director of the state mint and that Halilu was Aisha Buhari’s brother, while also listing other family/close-relatives appointments. This is one of the most material negative items for 7B. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Buhari’s actions contradict nepotism comment","publisher":"BusinessDay","publication_date":"2022-11-02","url":"https://businessday.ng/business-economy/article/buharis-actions-contradict-nepotism-comment/","claim":"The article says Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu’s appointment as NSPMC managing director, identifies Halilu as Aisha Buhari’s brother, and argues this fit a broader pattern of family and close-relative appointments.","locator":"paras. 79-88","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Mainstream Nigerian business press with a dated, specific appointment claim and direct attribution.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exactly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct presidential approval of a family-linked appointment; attribution is strong for the appointment, weaker for the broader pattern unless corroborated elsewhere.","contrary_evidence":["Halilu had relevant banking experience, which supporters used as a merit argument.","A family tie does not by itself prove self-enrichment, but it is strong evidence of favoritism risk."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10"]}`
- The ECOWAS Court ruling is a major negative item: it found the Buhari government’s Twitter suspension unlawful and ordered non-repetition. The same article notes the ban followed deletion of Buhari’s tweet, which gives the ruling a direct personal nexus. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Nigeria’s Twitter ban is unlawful– ECOWAS Court","publisher":"BusinessDay","publication_date":"2022-07-15","url":"https://businessday.ng/technology/article/nigerias-twitter-ban-is-unlawful-ecowas-court/","claim":"The ECOWAS Court held that the Buhari government’s Twitter suspension was unlawful and ordered Nigeria not to repeat it; the article links the ban to Twitter deleting Buhari’s tweet.","locator":"paras. 75-82","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent reporting on a court judgment with a clear legal outcome and identifiable causal context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022, while addressing the government action that carried over into the year.","ruler_attribution":"Strong ruler attribution through the presidency and the reported trigger involving Buhari’s own tweet.","contrary_evidence":["The government framed the suspension as a national-security response to fake news and subversion.","The court ruling does not itself prove Buhari personally authored every enforcement decision."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.8","7B.10"]}`
- The January 2022 lifting of the Twitter ban is the best corrective signal in the dossier. The government statement says Buhari approved ending the suspension after a technical committee recommendation. That is evidence of a reversal, but only after a six-month censorship episode and a court defeat later in the year. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"FULL TEXT: FG Statement As Buhari Approves Lifting Of Suspension On Twitter Operations In Nigeria","publisher":"Independent Nigeria","publication_date":"2022-01-12","url":"https://independent.ng/full-text-fg-statement-as-buhari-approves-lifting-of-suspension-on-twitter-operations-in-nigeria/","claim":"A federal government statement said Buhari approved lifting the Twitter suspension effective 13 January 2022 after a committee recommendation.","locator":"paras. 71-84 and 110-118","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"The published text reproduces the government statement and dates the approval and implementation clearly.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct presidential approval, though operationally carried out through NITDA and the ministerial committee.","contrary_evidence":["The suspension had already lasted months and was widely criticized as censorship.","The government’s stated security rationale was rejected by the later ECOWAS ruling."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.7","7B.8","7B.10"]}`
- The 2022 digital news report for Nigeria is useful context, not a direct ruler act: it says that after the Twitter ban was lifted, the Buhari government pushed proposed social-media regulation that drew backlash over media-freedom risks. This reinforces the pattern of pressure on scrutiny rather than a one-off event. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Nigeria","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publication_date":"2022-06-15","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2022/nigeria","claim":"The report says that after the Twitter ban was lifted in January 2022, the Buhari government pushed a proposed NBC social-media regulation bill that drew backlash over possible media-freedom infringement.","locator":"section on digital media and regulation after the Twitter ban","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"High-quality journalism scholarship, but the point is a synthesized media-environment assessment rather than a primary record.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly about the 2022 media environment under Buhari.","ruler_attribution":"Government-level attribution is strong; personal attribution to Buhari is indirect but still relevant because the policy came from his administration.","contrary_evidence":["This describes a proposed bill, not enacted censorship in itself.","The report is broader media-environment context rather than a single ruler act."],"lenses":["7B.7","7B.8","7B.10"]}`
- The 2022 academic paper on Buhari appointments is a useful secondary corroboration of patronage criticism. It argues that Buhari’s federal appointments were widely perceived as lopsided toward northern Muslim appointees and inconsistent with the federal-character principle. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Politics of Nepotism and National Integration in Nigeria: A Critical Analysis of Federal Appointments under President Muhammadu Buhari's Administration","publisher":"American Journal of Social and Humanitarian Research / ResearchGate copy","publication_date":"2022-12","url":"https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374664762_Politics_of_Nepotism_and_National_Integration_in_Nigeria_A_Critical_Analysis_of_Federal_Appointments_under_President_Muhammadu_Buhari%27s_Administration","claim":"The paper argues that Buhari’s federal appointments were widely perceived as lopsided toward northern Muslim appointees and inconsistent with federal-character norms.","locator":"discussion around lines 1033-1039, 1195-1199, and 1402-1411","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Academic-style analysis with explicit textual argument, but accessed through ResearchGate rather than the publisher site and relying on interpretive claims.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Published in 2022 and discussing Buhari’s then-current administration.","ruler_attribution":"Attribution is to Buhari’s appointment pattern; the evidence is interpretive and depends on the author’s synthesis.","contrary_evidence":["The paper is analytical, not a court finding or official audit.","Appointment diversity claims from official sources remain a counterpoint, though not enough to erase the criticism."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.9","7B.10"]}`

Search and rejection summary
- I considered roughly 30 documents across Reuters/Reuters-linked coverage, State House releases, BusinessDay, The Nation, Independent, Access Now, ECOWAS-court reporting, CPJ, Africa Check, and one 2022 academic paper.
- I retained the most material ruler-specific items and pruned near-duplicates on the same stories, especially repeated coverage of the Twitter ban and the Halilu appointment.
- I rejected or demoted several items because they were either too generic, not clearly ruler-specific, or mostly country-level context: media-environment summaries without a clear Buhari nexus, general corruption background, and broad claims about Nigeria’s corruption level.
- I also treated some items as context only, not final evidence, when they were mostly Buhari’s own self-description without external corroboration.
- I did not pull in out-of-period material where it was avoidable; when I used 2023/2024 references in other chapters earlier in the thread, I did not carry them forward here unless they directly illuminated the 2022 record.
- I did not rely on the client matrix as evidence.

Remaining gaps
- Direct evidence on Buhari’s personal assets, campaign finance, hidden conflicts, or private enrichment remains thin. More search in Code of Conduct Bureau records, asset-declaration reporting, and procurement/audit investigations would help.
- I have strong evidence on patronage and censorship, but less on deliberate falsehoods in Buhari’s own 2022 public statements beyond his self-serving end-of-term claims. More fact-checking of his 2022 speeches would help.
- The appointment evidence is strong on favoritism risk, but less decisive on whether those appointees were selected for competence or family access. More independent personnel-analysis reporting would help.
- I found clear evidence of suppression of scrutiny through the Twitter ban and journalist detentions, but less direct evidence tying every enforcement act personally to Buhari rather than his security apparatus. More primary court and administrative records would help tighten attribution.
